note: End-to-end paths for the toxic shock case. Steps cost eight seconds each on the runner's clock.

scenarios.name: Intended path: fluid, find and remove the tampon, antibiotics, norepinephrine when the fluid fades, intensive care
scenarios.note: The path the case is built around. It passes through the hypotensive phase on purpose.

scenarios.name: Intended path reaches the stabilizing phase before any handoff
scenarios.note: Fluid, source out, vasopressor after the fade.

scenarios.name: Doing nothing at all: hypotensive at five minutes, profound shock four minutes later
scenarios.note: The do-nothing path. It does not end the case.

scenarios.name: Doing nothing stops at hypotension if you stop the clock there
scenarios.note: First hop of the do-nothing path.

scenarios.name: Fluid alone: the response fades and more fluid does not rescue her
scenarios.note: Each bolus buys less. Without a vasopressor she progresses.

scenarios.name: One bolus moves her to the fluid-responsive phase after ten seconds
scenarios.note: Any crystalloid counts, through the coverage group.

scenarios.name: Sepsis treated, source missed: fluid, antibiotics and a vasopressor slow her and do not stop her
scenarios.note: The supported phase has a 270-second clock that only source removal cancels.

scenarios.name: The supported phase holds while its clock runs
scenarios.note: Fluid and a vasopressor with the tampon still in.

scenarios.name: Rescue from profound shock once the source is found
scenarios.note: Every deterioration in this case has an exit.

scenarios.name: Rescue one step short: in profound shock with the source out and no vasopressor
scenarios.note: Source removal alone does not lift her out. She still needs the vasopressor.

scenarios.name: A vasopressor started while she is fluid-responsive catches the fade
scenarios.note: Early vasopressor is accepted. She skips the hypotensive phase.

scenarios.name: Everything done early: she goes from fluid-responsive straight to stabilizing
scenarios.note: Epinephrine counts as a running vasopressor through coverage.

scenarios.name: Removing a foreign body is blocked until the pelvic examination has been done
scenarios.note: The blocked attempt sets no flag, so the source clock still runs out.

scenarios.name: A vasopressor without any fluid does not lift her out of hypotension
scenarios.note: The exit needs both. The nurse asks for fluid at 80 seconds.

scenarios.name: A vasopressor and then fluid in the hypotensive phase, source still in
scenarios.note: Order does not matter. Both flags together start the ten-second rule.

scenarios.name: Attempted discharge on arrival: she faints and the case continues
scenarios.note: attempt_discharge is the hidden action the Handoff tab logs when discharge is chosen early.

scenarios.name: Attempted discharge after one liter: she faints and the case continues
scenarios.note: The phase in which she looks most like a patient who could go home.

scenarios.name: After the faint she is recovered the same way as anyone else in the hypotensive phase
scenarios.note: Failure is recoverable.

scenarios.name: Dopamine is discouraged and still counts as a running vasopressor
Rate control does not change the phase
scenarios.note: Discouraged, with a vital effect. Covered siblings resolve to the same action.

scenarios.name: Antibiotics alone change nothing on the monitor
scenarios.note: Deliberate. No antibiotic moves a phase.

scenarios.name: Handoff from the hypotensive phase ends the case
Rescue inside the last window of the 300-second clock: a bolus before it fires
scenarios.note: Paired with the next scenario (authoring section 16 step 8). The bolus is logged at 286 seconds on the runner's clock.

scenarios.name: One action too late for the 300-second clock: the same bolus after it has fired
scenarios.note: The bolus goes in after 300 seconds. In the hypotensive phase fluid alone changes no phase.

scenarios.name: Rescue inside the last window of the 240-second clock: fluid added to a running vasopressor
scenarios.note: Hypotensive from 300 seconds, so the clock fires at 540. The bolus is logged before that.

scenarios.name: One action too late for the 240-second clock: the same fluid after it has fired
scenarios.note: Fluid and a vasopressor are both in, the source is not out, and from profound shock she needs all three.

scenarios.name: Rescue inside the last window of the 270-second clock: the source comes out before it fires
scenarios.note: Supported from 176 seconds on the runner's clock, so its clock fires at 446. The removal is logged at 432.

scenarios.name: A maintenance infusion is not a bolus: she still deteriorates at 300 seconds
scenarios.note: v0.24 audit. Neither infusion sets the fluid flag.

scenarios.name: Stopping a covered vasopressor is refused and she stays supported
scenarios.note: v0.24 audit. Stop Vasopressin was unbound. It is now covered by the stop action, which refuses.

scenarios.name: Stopping a vasopressor when none is running is blocked and changes nothing
scenarios.note: v0.24 audit. The prerequisite is a running vasopressor.

scenarios.name: Digoxin and amiodarone are rate control and do not change the phase
scenarios.note: v0.24 audit. Both are covered by the rate-control action.
